clue.text: Faithless folk witnessing robberies?

parts.note: someone witnessing an event is at it, present there
heists are robberies, especially daring ones

explanation.surface: Godless people looking on while banks are being robbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: people at heists would be witnessing robberies.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheists reject belief in any god, so they are literally without religious faith.

clue.text: Terrible state of duck in pasty I'd cooked

indicators.note: in places the zero-score letter inside the rearranged letters
cooked suggests the letters are prepared afresh, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: duck cooked inside a pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the cricket score of nothing, the letter O, not the bird; 'cooked' is the anagram signal and 'in' sets the O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dystopia is an imagined society where everything has gone dreadfully wrong, the opposite of utopia.

clue.text: True: sea can be cold

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A true observation that the sea can be chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges TRUE and SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: An austere manner is stern and unfriendly, which is what a cold person shows.

clue.text: Stout from barrel in bar

indicators.note: in puts the cask word inside the rod word

parts.note: a rod is a metal or wooden bar
a tun is a large cask or barrel for beer or wine

explanation.surface: Stout beer poured from a barrel in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' and 'barrel' and 'bar' all point to beer, but stout is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund and stout both describe a plump, round-bodied person.

clue.text: More work — increased touring to Italy and America

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rise word goes round the short word

parts.note: prices that have increased are up
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: More work after a rise in tours to Italy and America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, author of the book, not 'extra'; 'touring' signals one piece going round another.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More wrote Utopia (1516), describing an ideal island commonwealth.

clue.text: Is it your 25? I don't care for it

definitions.text: Is it your 25? I don't care for it

parts.words: Is it your 25? I don't care for it
parts.note: 25 across is a kind of tea; someone asked whether they like it replies with the idiom for disliking something

explanation.surface: An exchange: is this blend your favourite? No, I dislike it.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is EARL GREY, so the question asks whether it is your tea, and the reply turns down the tea and the idiom alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something you do not like, here literally a tea you dislike.

clue.text: Aorta and lung repaired to keep one in US force

indicators.note: to keep means the rearranged letters hold the numeral letter inside
repaired suggests the parts are put back together differently, so rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Surgeons repairing a patient's aorta and lung to keep them alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' is the anagram signal, and 'to keep' holds the I for one inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Guard is a reserve military force of the United States, organised by each state.

clue.text: Still together

definitions.meaning: still means nevertheless, which the phrase also means
together means simultaneously, happening at one moment

explanation.surface: Two words that both describe quiet companionship.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both simultaneously and nonetheless, matching each sense.

clue.text: A trial involving tense witness

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the trial word takes in the grammar letter

parts.note: a test is a trial
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A courtroom trial with a tense witness on the stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts T inside A TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness that something is true, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Advertises Spielberg classic, wearing best suit

indicators.note: wearing means the suit word is worn around the film letters

parts.note: in card games trumps is the suit that beats all others
E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial is a famous Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A film fan promotes a Spielberg classic while dressed in their finest suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best suit' is the card-game suit, not clothing; 'wearing' signals the film's letters sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim it loudly, much as an advertiser does.

clue.text: United were victorious according to report

indicators.note: according to report means as heard spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: won is the past tense of win, being victorious

explanation.surface: A football report saying Manchester United won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: People united are at one, joined as a single whole.

clue.text: Work close to pubs, drink slowly and chatter

parts.note: a machine that works goes

indicators.note: close to means the end, so the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to sip is to drink slowly in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: After work, near the pubs, people sip drinks and chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like nearness but means the last letter of 'pubs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle talk about other people, a kind of chatter.

clue.text: Angry-looking wine expert in France died

parts.note: red is a type of wine
F is the international vehicle code for France
an ace is an expert
d. is the abbreviation for died in records

explanation.surface: A wine expert in France has died, looking flushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being red-faced means flushed with anger or embarrassment, so it looks cross.

clue.text: Father covering round behind

indicators.note: covering means the father abbreviation wraps around the ring letter

parts.note: Fr is the short form of the title Father
a round shape is an O

explanation.surface: A father covering a round of drinks for his son behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' is backing, supporting, not rearward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being for a cause means backing or supporting it, the sense of being behind it.

clue.text: Tom's hand tool?

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male cat, and its hand is its paw
a person used by another to do unpleasant work is a tool or dupe

explanation.surface: A tomcat's paw described as a hand tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The fable of the monkey using a cat's paw to pull chestnuts from the fire gives the dupe sense.

clue.text: Mary Jane or Jerry?

definitions.meaning: Mary Jane is slang for marijuana
a jerry is British slang for a chamber ...

explanation.surface: Two names that look like a couple or cartoon characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Both names are slang, not people; a jerry is an old British word for a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis and also a chamber pot, so both sense fit.

clue.text: Crowd backed one short story to do with union

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the crowd word reads in reverse

parts.note: to ram is to crowd or cram things together
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: short means a letter is cut from the end of the word

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A crowd supports one short story about a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses RAM to MAR; 'short' trims TALE to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, the union of spouses.

clue.text: Primate consuming stew: it shows hunger

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the primate word swallows the other letters

parts.note: an ape is a primate
being in a stew is being in a pet, a fit of sulky temper

explanation.surface: An ape eating stew shows how hungry it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like food but means a sulk, PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is the desire for food, the same feeling as hunger.

clue.text: Score from fashionable old pen-pusher

parts.note: something fashionable is in
a scribe was a clerk who copied documents by hand in the past

explanation.surface: A musical score from a trendy old clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' is a verb, to mark by cutting, not music or a number.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut lines into it, which is to inscribe it.

clue.text: Removing restraints in county in Germany

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Unchaining prisoners in a county in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters inside 'county in Germany'.
explanation.definitionFit: Untying knots or bonds frees someone, taking off their restraints.

clue.text: Peaty gin mixed for Cleopatra say

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A cocktail of peaty gin served to Cleopatra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges PEATY GIN; 'say' marks Cleopatra as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was a queen of ancient Egypt, an example of an Egyptian.

clue.text: Pluck wings of excellent young chicken

parts.note: to pull feathers is to pluck them

indicators.note: the wings of something are its two sides, so the outer letters

explanation.surface: Plucking the wings of a fine young chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings of' takes the outer letters of 'excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullet is a young hen, under a year old.

clue.text: Flood ruins rebuilt hotel

indicators.note: rebuilt suggests the ruins are put together in another order

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A flood leaves ruins, and a hotel is rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges RUINS.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a sudden flowing in, as of water, much like a flood.

clue.text: Bill has correspondence with leading lady

parts.note: post is mail, correspondence
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, Britain's leading lady

explanation.surface: A man named Bill exchanges letters with a star actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is a printed notice; ER, the late Queen, is the leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice for public display, as in billposter.

clue.text: Ambassador on time finds article

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the title follows the time letter

parts.note: HE, His or Her Excellency, is the form of address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador on time finds an article in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is a grammar word, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The is the definite article in English grammar.

clue.text: Romeo in travelling eagerly finds brew

indicators.note: in puts the phonetic letter inside the rearranged letters
travelling suggests the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo travels eagerly and finds a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges EAGERLY, and 'in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a black tea flavoured with bergamot, which is brewed in a pot.

clue.text: Root posh sailors planted in dump

indicators.note: planted in means put into the ground, so these letters go inside the dump word

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump in British English
U means upper-class, posh
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Smart sailors root about in a rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' is a vegetable, not rummaging; 'planted in' puts the posh and sailors letters inside the dump word.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root vegetable.

clue.text: Tender lass struggling with big furniture item

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tender girl struggles with a big piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges TENDER LASS and BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing table is a bedroom piece of furniture with a mirror and drawers.
